blindSummary:
Three overseas municipalities are integral parts of a distant metropolitan state, whose national law - including marriage equality, applicable here since 2012 - applies in full, a regional outlier. The local deviation is social (small-island conservatism), not legal.

Risk is derived from the metropolitan state's legal framework, adjusted for a small-island conservative social climate; the underlying evidence base is that state's own law.
blindOutOfScope: Integral overseas part of the metropolitan state; local deviations per the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: Safety and travel page of the host city of the 2026 international Pride event (about the metropolitan state, included here because these overseas municipalities are an integral part of it): covers border/airport procedures, the visa-free-area rule that foreign nationals must carry passports, main-airport logistics, and a dedicated section for transgender and non-binary visitors. Notes the metropolitan state sits in the upper-middle band of a 2026 regional legal-rights index.

International LGBT-rights organisation overview of the metropolitan state (updated March 2026): progressive laws with gaps - legal gender change still requires a medical expert letter; nonbinary 'X' marker only via a 3-9 month court procedure; the metropolitan state's self-ID gender law was withdrawn in July 2025. The three overseas municipalities follow the metropolitan state's law directly as fully integrated territories.

International trans-rights organisation's global legal-mapping report 2019 (3rd edition): maps legal gender recognition laws and policies by country/territory - includes these three fully integrated overseas municipalities, which follow the metropolitan state's legal gender recognition framework.
LGBT travel site (Dec 2022): a top-ten list of regional destinations where same-sex marriage is legal - travel-oriented overview for couples planning destination weddings.

Regional legal-information portal (Dec 2012): the first same-sex wedding in these overseas municipalities, performed on one of the three islands for two visiting residents - that island was the first of the metropolitan state's former overseas federation to facilitate same-sex weddings after a 2010 change of constitutional status.

Official tourism page of the same island: markets it for destination weddings (civil ceremonies in the historic council chamber, flexible registrar) - relevant because same-sex marriages are performed there under the metropolitan state's law.
